items.q: How were hidden cuts in Dream's Manhunt videos found?
items.a: Tells in **simulation state**: HUD, smelt times, glint, hunger-bar phase — not obvious **jump-cut frames**.

items.q: Why was the furnace a giveaway?
items.a: Iron ore takes **200 ticks (10 seconds)** to smelt. The clip produced **more ingots than the elapsed time** allowed.

items.q: What does 'lag' mean in a game engine?
items.a: Not one thing: a missed **frame budget**, a late **GPU**, or **client prediction** meeting delayed server packets.

items.q: Why should effects use game time, not wall-clock time?
items.a: So recorded runs **replay exactly**, and so a hidden cut does not make the effect **jump**.

items.q: How did analysts recover the exact tick from a video?
items.a: The hunger bar's bob is a **PRNG of the tick**. Work backwards from the pattern, then flag **timeline gaps**.

items.q: What is Casey's warning about data-driven game data?
items.a: Tunables belong in **data, not code**, but do not data-drive **too early**, and do not use **JSON as a runtime format**.

sections.title: Why it is a programming lesson

items.q: What is the reusable skill here?
items.a: **Engine primitives** (ticks, clocks, netcode, PRNGs) turn a drama claim into a **testable timeline**.
**Open-source computer vision** that reads the hunger-bar region and **maps it back to a tick**.

items.q: What did a spliced clutch reveal?
items.a: The hot bar **saw into the future** — a composite, not a single uncut take.
